questions.question: Using the scooter purchase of R24 000 for cash, explain why a transaction with zero net effect on the accounting equation still requires two entries.
questions.expected_answer: Two real changes happened: Vehicles, an asset, increased by R24 000 and Bank, an asset, decreased by R24 000. Each change must be recorded — debit Vehicles, credit Bank. The equation is unchanged only because the two entries cancel inside assets; the zero net effect is the result of the two entries, not a reason to omit them.

questions.question: Show the verification of the accounting equation for Naidoo Stationers after all four transactions, naming each figure.
questions.expected_answer: Assets: Bank R50 000 (R80 000 in, R24 000 and R6 000 out) plus Vehicles R24 000 plus Trading Stock R15 000 equals R89 000. Owner's equity: Capital R80 000. Liabilities: Creditors R9 000 (R15 000 less R6 000 paid). O plus L is R80 000 plus R9 000, which is R89 000, equal to total assets — the equation balances.

questions.question: Explain where incomes and expenses fit into the accounting equation, and use the payment of R1 800 wages as your example.
questions.expected_answer: Incomes and expenses are not a fourth element; they are movements inside owner's equity. Income increases owner's equity and is credited; expenses decrease owner's equity and are debited. Paying wages of R1 800 means Bank, an asset, decreases — credit Bank — and owner's equity decreases through the Wages expense — debit Wages.
